newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Vietnam's Mekong Delta fights serious flooding.
newsitem.headline: Vietnam's Mekong Delta fights serious flooding.

text.p: Flooding in southern Vietnam's Mekong Delta has spread across eight provinces, killing 64 people and placing more than two million in need of help, relief workers said on Tuesday.
An official with the International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies in Ho Chi Minh City said 52 of the dead were children.
"We heard about a teacher today. She could swim but drowned when currents washed her away," he said.
Provincial officials met relief workers on Tuesday to discuss the situation and reported some 2,375,000 people needed help, including 54,530 families facing serious food shortages.
"Water levels are slightly down on the Cambodian border but it's getting worse in lower provinces," the IFRC official said.
He added that more than 120,000 people had been evacuated from their homes so far, and local authorities were planning to move nearly 237,000 others.
Flooding in the lower stretches of the Mekong, one of Southeast Asia's major rivers, is becoming an annual problem and has claimed hundreds of lives in recent years.

Environmentalists say the situation is getting worse because of deforestation in upstream catchment areas and the diversion of natural water channels for farming in the heavily populated lower stretches of the river.
This year's flooding is said to be the worst in more than two decades, but damage and casualties so far are lighter than in both 1995 and 1994 when hundreds died.
Officials say early harvesting of rice crops and better preparation has helped but they have also warned that the long-term impact of flooding for a third year in a row is not yet known.
